title: The Third Witness
premise: True-crime podcaster Sebastian Brightwater receives a confession letter for the forty-year-old Brightwater Cove drowning case — postmarked the day after the last witness's funeral, and signed with her own family name. Returning to the decaying seaside town that raised her, she discovers the letter is one of three, each witness holding a piece of a night the town agreed to forget. As she records her final season, loyalty to the aunt who raised her collides with the truth: the drowning was no accident, and the inheritance that saved her childhood was bought with silence. In the climax, the tide gives up what it took — a locket proving which of the three witnesses actually pulled the trigger of fate — and Sebastian must choose between exposing her own blood or letting the sea keep its secret. She broadcasts the truth, loses her aunt, but gains a found family among those who finally stop lying.
about_author: Ada Ashgrove spent a decade as a court stenographer in coastal towns before turning to fiction, giving her an ear for the things people almost say. She writes mysteries about families whose secrets are older than their houses.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Days after wrapping her podcast's most popular season, she opens a confession to the Brightwater Cove drowning — signed 'E.B.,' her estranged aunt Edith's initials. The letter claims the death wasn't accidental and names two other witnesses. Emotional beat: dread laced with longing, as the case she's chased professionally turns out to be personally hers.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Back in Brightwater Cove, she interviews the second witness, harbor master Cole Fenwick, who denies everything while slipping her his copy of a matching letter. Her aunt refuses to speak, burning papers at night. Rising tension: someone ransacks Sebastian's rental and steals the first letter. Beat: the warmth of small-town welcome curdling into surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, shifting briefly to Edith's flashback. A storm uncovers the drowned man's belongings; inside is a locket holding a photograph that contradicts every official account. Edith finally confesses she saw everything — but swears she wasn't the one who let him drown. Climax builds: the third witness, revealed to be Sebastian's late grandfather, orchestrated the cover-up and the inheritance. Beat: betrayal at the heart of found family.

chapters.title: Three Letters, One Truth
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Confronting Cole at the breakwater, she gets the full confession recorded as the tide rises; he nearly silences her, but Edith arrives and stands between them. Sebastian airs the final episode, naming all three witnesses including her grandfather. Resolution: Edith leaves town in disgrace yet reconciles partially with Sebastian; Cole turns himself in; the town, stripped bare, begins honestly rebuilding. Beat: grief transmuted into belonging.
